Panj-i Al-i Aba (the Incident of the Cloak): Who are the Ahl al-Bayt?
hook: One morning in Medina, the Prophet left his house and gathered five people under a blanket. He calls them "Ahl al-Bayt". Who are these five?
scenes.0.text: One morning, the Prophet (peace be upon him) left his house with a black woolen cloth wrapped around his shoulders and called his family to him. This meeting took place at the house of the Prophet's wife Umm Salamah. The first to arrive was his grandson, **Hasan**. The Prophet took her under his veil. Then his younger brother Husayn came and he was brought in with his grandfather. Then came the Prophet's daughter, **Fatima**. Finally, **Ali** has arrived. The Prophet took all four of them under his cloak and covered it over them. And when the five were gathered together under the same covering, the Prophet recited the verse 33:33: "Allah only desires to remove the filth from you, O people of the House, and to purify you".

scenes.1.text: The Prophet raised his hands to those under the veil and said, "O Allah, these are my people. Remove the filth from them and purify them". **Ummu Seleme** was at home at the time and heard this prayer. And he desired to share in the honour, and he turned to the veil and said, "O Messenger of Allah, am I with them?" The Prophet didn't break it and said, "You're on good terms". But he didn't open the curtain for her. Umm Salamah was a noble wife of the Prophet, and she confirmed the Prophet's word that he was on the right path. Yet that morning, under the veil, there was only the Prophet, **Ali**, **Fatima**, **Hasan** and Husayn.

scenes.2.text: This verse is called Ayat-i Tathir. Tathir means cleansing from filth. The word "household" here refers to the household. The Prophet did not recite this verse upon a random group. He read over the five men he had taken under his cloak with his hands and prayed for them. In Shia reading, this purification means that they are protected from sin and error. It's called a name. The Imamate, the guidance of Allah, is based on this purity. And whoever guides them must be one whom Allah has purified. All subsequent imams are descended from the family beneath the veil.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.text: Years after the Prophet's death, Zeid b. Erkam was asked who the Ahl al-Bayt were. Zeid kept the Prophet's wives out of this close circle. Then he counted the families from whom they were forbidden to take the zakat: the families of **Ali**, Aqil, Ja'far and **Abbas**. This was a long list of the Prophet's extended family. But right in the middle of the list were five people gathered under the covers that morning. Zeyd's answer was that the word Ahl al-Bayt referred to the Prophet's blood relatives. In Shia reading, the heart of this large ring is the five people under the veil.
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul

scenes.4.text: The Shiites call these five **Pence-i Al-i Aba**. Pence means five in Persian. Al-i Aba means family of the veil. These five are the Prophet, **Ali**, **Fatimah**, **Hasan** and Husayn. The open hand sign seen on Shiite houses, mourning flags, and tomb doors represents these five. Every finger reminds me of a name. When a child first sees this hand, he sees only one shape. His parents teach him five names one by one. In time, that hand becomes a sign in the child's eyes of both love and the tears shed at Karbala.

scenes.5.text: In the Ahl-i Beyt narratives, this event is narrated in a longer form than **Fatimah**. This narrative is called Hadith-i Kisa. Kisa is Arabic for cover. When five people are gathered under this veil, God presents these five to His angels. And Gabriel asks permission to come down to earth and get under the veil. Hadith-i Kisa is recited in Shiite homes, especially at wishes and prayer meetings. When it's being read, people bow their heads, spread their hands, and pray for these five. Shiites believe that wishes will be granted at these councils.

scenes.6.text: Hadis-i Kisa shows the nucleus of the Ahl-i Bayt. This core is the five people under the veil. All eleven imams after **Ali** are descendants of Ali and Fatimah, with **Hasan** and Husayn in the lead. That morning in Medina, in a house, there was a quiet moment witnessed by a few people. At Ghadir Hum, in front of thousands of pilgrims, the Prophet would raise the hand of one of these five, Ali. He covered it up, showed me who your family was. And Ghadir would announce to everyone who would be the leader of that family.

sunni.0.says: Aisha: the Prophet takes Imam Hasan, Imam Husayn, Fatima and Imam Ali under a black cloak and recites Ahzâb 33:33.
sunni.1.says: The Prophet prays for those under the cloak, "these are my Ahl al-Bayt"; Umm Salama asks, "and I?"
sunni.2.says: The scope of the Ahl al-Bayt: the families to whom zakat is forbidden; the wives are in the debate over this scope.
shia.0.says: The chains of the Kisa incident in Shia and Sunni sources; the relation of the long Hadith al-Kisa.
shia.1.says: The isma interpretation of Ahzâb 33:33 and the scope of the Ahl al-Bayt.
disputes.0.title: 1ayy4z2
The scope of the Ahl al-Bayt
disputes.0.sunni: The Prophet took Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under the cloak and recited Ahzâb 33:33. In the Sunni reading the scope is wider; the wives and the Banu Hashim also belong to the Ahl al-Bayt, the Kisa circle is the core, and the verse is among the verses addressing the wives.
disputes.0.shia: The Prophet took Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under the cloak and recited Ahzâb 33:33. In the Shia view the Verse of Purification and the Kisa hadith limit the Ahl al-Bayt who possess isma to the Prophet, Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn; the imams are of their lineage.
disputes.1.title: rfcilz
Umm Salama and the cloak
disputes.1.sunni: The Prophet did not take Umm Salama under the cloak and said to her, "You are on the good." In the Sunni reading this saying does not exclude her; it announces that she is on goodness and does not remove the view that the wives are counted among the Ahl al-Bayt.
disputes.1.shia: The Prophet did not take Umm Salama under the cloak and said to her, "You are on the good." In the Shia view, his not taking her under the cloak and keeping her apart shows that the verse specially means the five who possess isma.
questions.0: When Umm Salamah asked, "Am I with them?" the Prophet said, "You are in good health". Why do you think the Prophet only took these five under his veil?
questions.1: Zeyd b. When asked who the Ahl al-Bayt were, he kept the Prophet's wives out and counted the families from which they were forbidden to take zakat. Why do you think Zeid described the Ehl-i-Bayt as blood relatives?
questions.2: The prophet Ahaz read Psalm 33:33 not to a random group of people but to five men who were covered with his own hands. Why do you think it is important to determine who the "people" are?
summary: The Prophet took Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under the cloak and named them the Ahl al-Bayt. These five are Panj-i Al-i Aba and, in the Shia view, the core of the Ahl al-Bayt who possess isma.
key: Panj-i Al-i Aba: the five lights under the cloak
notes.0: The Kisa incident is related from Aisha in Muslim 2424.
notes.1: The Prophet took Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under a black cloak.
notes.2: Then he recited the verse «God only wants to remove impurity from you, O Ahl al-Bayt» (Ahzâb 33:33).
notes.3: These five are called «Panj-i Al-i Aba» (the five of the people of the cloak).
notes.4: These five under the cloak are the core of the Ahl al-Bayt in the Ja'fari school. The common account is these five people.
